$comment: The EuropeDoor palette, as data rather than as prose. tools/checks.py recomputes the WCAG 2.2 contrast of every pair below and fails the build if a role claimed here is not one the colour can actually hold. A palette written only in a document is a palette that drifts: a hex nudged 'slightly warmer' in a redesign takes a contrast ratio with it, and nothing complains until somebody cannot read a link.
philosophy: European Future — editorial x architectural x cinematic x intelligent

discover.role: Light, warm, editorial, human. Where people fall in love with Europe: photography, culture, food, journeys, cities.

intelligence.role: Dark, graphite, luminous. Where people interact with the machine: maps, routes, planning, personalisation, live information.

ratio.$comment: The ratio is the instruction, not the hex codes. Blue website plus gold buttons is what you get from a palette; European editorial design plus futuristic infrastructure is what you get from a ratio.

graphite.name: Deep Graphite
graphite.role: the technological foundation; ink in the light world, ground in the dark

graphite-2.name: Graphite Surface
graphite-2.role: cards and raised surfaces in the dark world

ivory.name: Warm Ivory
ivory.role: the main surface. Never pure white — white is a screen, ivory is paper

cobalt.name: European Cobalt
cobalt.role: the signature. Used sparingly and never as a background

cobalt-deep.name: Cobalt Deep
cobalt-deep.role: links and actions in the light world, where the signature is too light to read on stone

cobalt-lift.name: Cobalt Lift
cobalt-lift.role: links and actions in the dark world. Lifted 24% toward white rather than the 15% that first cleared AA on the ground: the raised surface #1A1E22 is lighter than the ground, so a value chosen against the ground alone falls to 4.07:1 on a card and fails. A dark palette has two backgrounds and the lighter one is the one that binds.

lime.name: Electric Lime
lime.role: the future accent. Dark world only — see the contrast table

ultramarine.name: Ultramarine
ultramarine.role: atmosphere only: gradients, map washes, immersive moments. Never text

forbidden.why: 3.52 — a UI edge at most, and never a link. Use cobalt-lift.
1.05 — invisible. Lime does not exist in the light world.
4.13 — fails body text. Ultramarine is atmosphere, never type.
3.13 — the dark world's link colour is a UI edge at most on light. Use cobalt-deep.

never: navy and gold as the primary pair
generic tourism blue as a page background
gold or brass on anything interactive
gradient as decoration rather than as atmosphere
the letters A and I in the masthead, the navigation, or any h1
